name: c-the-only-still-thing
prompt: A nineteenth-century glass-plate studio photograph, printed in cold silver-grey, of a city park bench seen straight on from bench height, full figure, deep focus. On the bench sits a stout rich man in a tall silk top hat, frock coat strained over his belly, gold watch chain, one gloved hand raised in a lazy wave of dismissal. He alone is rendered razor sharp: every stitch, the shine on his hat, a fixed smile held a little too wide and too long, pale eyes that never blinked through the whole exposure. The shutter stayed open for what looks like a century in daylight, so everything that moved has dissolved: translucent smears of soldiers on crutches, nurses in scrubs, crowds, prams, pigeons and falling leaves pass through the frame and through each other as faint grey ghost trails, some walking straight through the seat beside him, none of them solid enough to cast a shadow, while his own shadow under the bench is black and crisp. Flat overcast light, no contrast in the sky. The plate is decaying: a bluish metallic mirror sheen creeping in from the edges, fine hairline scratches, dust specks, a chipped lower corner showing clear glass, a faint crack network in the emulsion. The top third is an empty, blown-out, almost white sky with a few bare branches, quiet and clean. Unsettling stillness, a portrait of the one thing that never left. No text or lettering anywhere. Thanks.
